worksheet.text:
# Form-field tagged DOM/motion remediation — isolated proposal

Patch `form-field-dom-remediation-v1.patch` SHA-256 `35c6b6c0370af33e5e6d8dccc7ae05fa74cabee53cbb2024dec3e5b0268edcbc`, based on `7d59a0d2e1791046dc5cc6ad1aa472a8c0047a28`, applies with `git apply --check` to canonical `87a5f17d736f05154bb65e2f63a76347718d65a3`. The patch omits the separate reviewed menu product/test fix already present on that canonical head; it updates the shared resting-style test for that exact menu fix and for the form-field change. The isolated worktree contains those two menu changes solely for the combined style test.

The original is authenticated 16.2.14 source at `strong-focus-full-seal/tagged-16/src/material/legacy-form-field/{form-field.html,form-field.scss}` and `src/material/form-field/form-field-animations.ts`, commit `df60e733c60e572ba538f6ad0ceff3e63e527b53`. The tagged template has conditional direct child divs, with `mat-form-field-hint-wrapper` only for hint; error is an unclassed direct div whose `mat-error` directive supplies aria-live polite and aria-atomic true. The proposal removes the permanent message wrapper and all new subscript selector rules, recreates those two branches using existing control flow, and retains error host semantics and described-by. It introduces no CSS selector or Angular animation-engine dependency.

Engine-free motion uses the native `Element.animate` API on the newly rendered direct child after view checking. It restores the tagged inline resting `opacity:1` and `translateY(0%)`, uses tagged 300ms cubic-bezier and keyframe endpoints, and cancels superseded/destroyed effects. It does not retain fill-forwards: later consumer style changes are not masked by a completed effect. On browsers lacking `Element.animate`, it leaves the tagged final style and performs no animation. `AfterViewChecked` is the new Angular API use; installed exact-minimum `@angular/core` 22.1.7 `types/core.d.ts:3344` exposes the public nondeprecated `ngAfterViewChecked` lifecycle interface (file SHA-256 `7d9eea93a0ccb308851fe7b50af8b8d894e8f0ae456e339fe8dcd87bf3fcfd84`). This new use and changed form-field source need C04 source-evidence succession; the previous 33-use admission does not silently transfer.

A fresh offline reference Angular/Material 16.2.14 Chromium app was run with BrowserAnimationsModule and NoopAnimationsModule, zoneful. The Material and CDK cached 16.2.14 archives match SRI from the retained `reference/material-16.2.14/environment-package-lock.json`. `form-field-dom-reference16/{trace-result.json,trace-noop-result.json}` each SHA-256 `96a1b8ef688c8294dc00a65e298ddfd1cdeda99e121fe4436acd9a837eccac9c`: initial hint, error, restored hint each have one direct div; hint carries the historical hint class, error has no authored class, error host supplies live/atomic, and resting opacity/matrix are 1/identity. Reference Angular engine's generated `ng-trigger`, `ng-trigger-transitionMessages`, `ng-tns-*`, `ng-star-inserted` classes and structural comments are not reproduced; the tagged authored element/class structure is preserved. A scoped Cyph source search found no subscript-wrapper selector, but arbitrary consumers could select those generated classes; that compatibility difference is not proven absent outside the searched sources. These traces are not tagged SSR or a full baseline app qualification.

The candidate tarball `form-field-dom-artifact-v6/ngx-compat-material-legacy-22.0.0-rc.0.tgz` SHA-256 `539c472f5207e7d4f5be84dd18547c22265ac6845dfef55914429844e3b2c714` was built with pinned Node24 in the dirty isolated tree; source map content for the form-field TS hashes to current `ea2bcd2a85cb1511cfa57a7d68d2edd45757ecd703df0ebfa0d613e3f4b79ccd`. It predates the separately integrated menu patch, so it is not a clean final combined artifact. Do not infer full source/pack provenance from that source-map comparison alone.

- Chromium149 packed `form-field-dom-browser-v7/result.json` SHA-256 `364763227843765ed1a8f948cb43d6f409f7151a4d2a3ecd59f985c3cdc7fca7` passes eight motion/boundary/nested cases, zoneful/zoneless/noop/initial error. Checks include direct div/class, replacement, initial no animation, interpolation at explicit currentTime, rapid cancellation with caught AbortError, same-kind coalescing, active destruction, nested ownership, unsupported animate fallback and completed-effect consumer-style changes. This is not wall-clock, other-engine or full matrix proof.
- `form-field-dom-token-v7/result.json` SHA-256 `9086be3e3a0dc952b063e3c89de4af9b92f34ed48e4df653e94a68301a79ee67` passes four real Angular provider combinations including explicit Noop versus Material-disabled precedence, active cancellation and no error after destruction.
- `form-field-dom-ssr-v6/result.json` SHA-256 `d483227ef855f4c3e4ef944f3b00fb363fabde5d7d30bd68c25190292190600f` passes Angular22 server-render hint/error/hint, recreation, described-by, error live attributes, zero instrumented geometry and animation calls, and teardown. No hydration claim.
- `form-field-dom-native-smoke-v3.json` SHA-256 `91917e352a3c94ffbdf3587f5944c762c366c57b0bd3c45f31dc358fc43e72dc` passes six actual shared-consumer form-field cases on Chromium149: zoneful/zoneless × enabled/provider-disabled/reduced; reports 300ms/one native effect when enabled and zero effects disabled, no manual detectChanges. This is not the complete native matrix.
- `form-field-dom-style-v3.json` SHA-256 `aeac58ecbe90778f4478ebfeb94e1e90568c22deb703d31ba6c42b6225bc9038` passes 12 complete historical/public-native resting CSS comparisons and 22 negative controls, including restoring each removed menu hider and an unwanted form-field selector. Both peer arguments were the installed 22.1.7 peer, so the second label is not an independently exercised 21.x peer. Tagged sources remain untouched; no golden or exception was broadened.
- `node scripts/motion-smoke-regressions.mjs` and `node scripts/native-motion-regressions.mjs` pass (46 and 306 roster cases respectively). The latter explicitly rejects an obsolete wrapper and wrong enabled/disabled native-effect count. Earlier v4 cancellation assertion failed because it checked before scheduled view destruction; the test was corrected to wait for removal, with the same cancellation requirement, and v7 passes. Failed logs remain retained.

The patch does not alter consumer styles or publish. Fresh clean packed/full historical and browser matrices, independent candidate review, and source-bound admission successors for form-field, native motion and the changed resting-style producer are still required. WAAPI completion/style behavior is deliberately tested but other browser implementations, multiple error messages/screen-reader announcement behavior and dynamic preference changes are not fully qualified by these cases.

independent_review.text:
# Independent form-field DOM and motion review

Subject: isolated patch `form-field-dom-remediation-v1.patch`, SHA-256 `35c6b6c0370af33e5e6d8dccc7ae05fa74cabee53cbb2024dec3e5b0268edcbc`, against `87a5f17d736f05154bb65e2f63a76347718d65a3`. Applying the patch independently succeeded. Its form-field TS, HTML, SCSS SHA-256 values are `ea2bcd2a85cb1511cfa57a7d68d2edd45757ecd703df0ebfa0d613e3f4b79ccd`, `2dd63d98dcc0a2305b34df9c07d67e0329ae911a97a417a6738952ca3d76c93c`, and `1b80f7d539c8bea5647377e10fd380f03239e1d7ed7c101052b9b26f4c45cee8`. The v6 packed artifact SHA-256 is `539c472f5207e7d4f5be84dd18547c22265ac6845dfef55914429844e3b2c714`; its source map independently contained exactly the named TS and HTML hashes. It predates the separate menu fix; form-field bytes are unchanged, but it is not a fresh combined artifact.

The untouched Material 16.2.14 HTML has direct conditional error and hint divs, the latter carrying `mat-form-field-hint-wrapper`. The candidate restores those Material-owned nodes and removes its nonhistorical permanent subscript wrapper and corresponding extra SCSS. The 16.2.14 transition metadata is a 300ms `cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 0.55, 0.2)` enter transition from opacity 0 and translateY(-5px) to opacity 1 and translateY(0%). Both original Material/CDK npm tarballs match exact committed reference lock SRIs. Independently reran the reference BrowserAnimations and NoopAnimations Chromium bundles; each produced identical reference trace SHA-256 `96a1b8ef688c8294dc00a65e298ddfd1cdeda99e121fe4436acd9a837eccac9c`. Initial hint, error, and restored hint had direct nodes and an opacity 1 / identity transform; the error host retained aria-live polite and aria-atomic true. The final candidate explicitly sets the same resting styles.

The author's v7 packed probe result covers zoneful, zoneless and Noop motion; hint/error/rapid replacement; cancellation including rejected finished promises; coalescing; active destruction; unsupported animate; completed effects and later consumer style changes; and nested ownership. Token policy probes cover four states. The candidate SSR probe checks hint/error, a11y IDs, no server animation or geometry calls and destruction; it does not establish tagged SSR or hydration parity. The author's six-case native Chromium motion smoke covers zoneful/zoneless enabled, provider disabled and reduced modes. Author's style report compares 12 cases and rejects 22 mutations; all six `--main-root` candidate source hashes independently matched this patched worktree. The original tagged resources remain pinned and no golden or selector exception was broadened.

Independent controls on copies of the v6 compiled zoneful browser bundle: unchanged positive passed; changing only the enter duration 300→301ms failed `historical timing changed`; replacing the resting identity transform with `none` failed `tagged resting transform`. These are fixture/bundle fault controls, not independent packed builds or upstream mutants. Logs live in `form-field-independent-negative-v1/`. Independently ran native-motion regressions (306 synthetic cases), lifecycle self-check (46), and motion smoke regressions (46); all passed. The added common checks bind exact visible element selector and animation count rather than accepting a background wrapper.

Boundaries: tagged Angular 16 also emits `ng-trigger`, `ng-trigger-transitionMessages`, `ng-star-inserted`, and generated `ng-tns-*` bookkeeping classes absent from this engine-free candidate. Root's decision is to preserve Material-owned structure/classes and behavior without synthesizing private engine markers; this is not byte-identical DOM. A scoped `~/cyph` search found no changed-subscript selector; it does not establish arbitrary consumer selector compatibility. SSR is candidate-tested only; hydration, tagged SSR parity, other engines, all appearances and the full native motion matrix remain outside this review. The user's private ownership restrictions are preserved. Final acceptance and fresh combined packed verification remain with the owner.

Conclusion: no additional concrete blocker within the reviewed Material-owned form-field DOM and bounded Chromium motion scope, subject to the explicit generated-marker difference and limitations above. No G11, full browser, release or security clearance is claimed.

root_decision: Restore Material16-owned direct hint/error nodes, hint class, error host ARIA and tagged inline resting opacity/identity transform. Native Element.animate owns only finite300ms enter interpolation; canceled when superseded/destroyed, no retained fill effect, missing-native-API fallback retains final styles. Preserve engine-free plan without synthesizing private/generated Angular animation or structural marker classes; this is not byte-identical engine-generated DOM. Existing context-scoped query preserves nested ownership.
scope_limits: No CSS/SCSS change required in ~/cyph; scoped search is not an exhaustive consumer build. Full plan, security and G11 remain incomplete.
